content: Recovered target: for every nonnegative k, sum_{j=0}^k 2^{k-j} binom(k+j,j)=4^k. Fact graph and global memory initially empty. Strong route: count length-(2k+1) binary words having more H than T. If the (k+1)-st H occurs at position k+j+1, then first k+j positions have k H and j T (binom(k+j,j) choices), the next is H, and the remaining k-j positions are arbitrary (2^{k-j} choices). Summing j=0..k counts all H-majority words uniquely. Swapping H and T is a fixed-point-free bijection between H-majority and T-majority words because length is odd, so exactly half of 2^{2k+1} words are H-majority, namely 2^{2k}=4^k.
